21   General information
This is a general description for the conveyor belt controls of a washing
line. The version depends on the individual machine line components, so
that your machine line may differ from the examples shown.
This operating manual provides information about the basic features,
operating methods and applications of the machine, furthermore, it con-
tains all information required for safe and proper operation.
1.1  Safety instructions – General

nResidual risks
The machine/machine line complies with the valid standards, laws
and the current state-of-the-art but not all residual risks can be rem-
edied by structural measures. For this reason, always adhere to all
safety and warning notes. Otherwise, there is the danger of injuries
or damage to assets.
nWarning notes
Warning notes inform about the type of danger, the consequences of
non-observance and the possible measures for remedy prior to
starting any actions.
nIt is not possible to consider every case in the warning notes
Safety is always a matter of common sense and your own experi-
ence. There are safety rules of a general character which have to be
observed at all times. Furthermore, every situation has its own spe-
cial characteristics.

Only use the machine/machine line according to its intended use.
For detailed information about the intended use of this machine/

system on the air servicing unit.

6nFurther measures:
–  Ensure that all drives are at a standstill.
–  Prior to opening any sections of the compressed air system,
depressurize the machine.

assembly groups to suitable load lifting gear.

71.3  Obligations of the user/owner
The machine/machine line is built according to the state of the art and is
operationally safe. This does not rule out that hazards could emanate
from the machine/machine line or damage occur to the machine/machine
line.
For this reason, the user/owner has to guarantee that:
nAll persons instructed to install, operate, maintain, repair, dismantle
or dispose of this machine/machine line must have read and under-
stood the parts of the operating manual pertaining to their work prior
to performing this work. Have all persons confirm that they have
understood the operating manual by signing the »Printed form for
training persons with/on the machine/machine line« form.
nThis operating manual must always be kept within easy reach.
nWrite an operating instruction for the machine operators and provide
it at the workplace on the machine/machine line.
nEnsure that the machine/machine line and all of its safety devices/
guards are always functional.
nAll scheduled maintenance/inspections must be performed within the
specified time intervals.
nEnsure that no modifications, attachments or conversions to/on the
machine line are made without the manufacturer's permission.
nAdhere to the regulations concerning the Employer's Liability Insur-
ance Association! These are in particular regulations laid down by
the Employers' Liability Insurance Companies for the branches tex-
tile/clothing and laundry, national standards/laws and EC directives.

covers and similar materials) the weight of which does not exceed the

automatically.

manufacturer does not assume any liability for injury to
persons or damage to the machine caused by use other
than that intended.

10.1.1.1    Conveyor belt positioning
Laser path measuring systems, conventional position switches or incre-
mental encoders in connection with frequency converters can be used to
position the conveyor belts.
Fig. 119: Lift shuttle versions (example)
1Lift shuttles with position measurement by means of a laser
2Lift shuttles with position measurement by means of a incremental
encoder
The conveyor belt traversing speed depends on the current distance
between the conveyor belt and the target position: The greater the dis-
tance, the faster the conveyor belt traversing speed and vice versa.
The current position is determined via pulse lasers with runtime meas-
uring.
The laser for the horizontal position is fastened to the traverse rail and
the one for the vertical position (if available) on the traversing frame.
For this measuring method, the spacing between the conveyor belt and
the laser is continuously measured and transmitted to the PLC via an
analogue interface (Input 0-10V).
There the possible travel and lifting positions are saved and transmitted
as set point values to software controllers depending on the current
target position.
Then positioning takes place via a further analogue interface (Output
0-10V) or CAN interface by means of frequency converters with asyn-
chronous motors as actuators. The current measured values are dis-
played in the individual view.

109Information about function and commissioning/start-up
Laser:
The light beam emitted by the laser and, thus, the visible light point must
hit the reflector center.
Ensure that the light point position does not change decisively neither at
the minimum nor at the maximum spacing between conveyor belt and
laser and, in particular, is not located near the reflector edge. Ensure that
no other material is located between the laser and the reflector.
Adjust the rotary potentiometer for the zero point calibration (bottom
potentiometer) such that a path between 50 (mm) and the limit value
20000 or 40000 (mm) is visible for the entire possible travel zone of the
conveyor belt in the display of the operating device (manual operation).
The correctness of the absolute value of the measured path is not rele-
vant for the control system because the measured values are only rela-
tive positions related to the default set point values.
The RH (red) LED signals a laser malfunction and must not be lit in the
entire travel zone.
Laser measurement can be parameterized within the configuration
menu. There, the determination is made for which movement direction a
laser measurement is available, whether the laser is fitted from the LH or
RH side related to the conveyor belt and which laser type (20m or 40m
measuring range) is used.
If the supply voltage for the laser fluctuates below 24VDC, this will result
in measuring inaccuracies. If possible, connect the transformer on the
mains side such that the supply voltage reliably exceeds 24VDC.
Frequency converter
For checking or changing the parameters, refer to the detailed informa-
tion in the frequency converter operating manual.
The frequency set point value is transmitted to the frequency converter
as an 0-10V analogue signal by the PLC. The rotational direction is
transmitted by the PLC via two digital release outputs. Check these three
signal lines for function, if problems are encountered. For this, any move-
ment direction can be preset in manual mode and the signal behavior
can be checked.
For a frequency-controlled drive motor change the phases behind the
frequency converter to change the rotational direction.

10.1.1.3    Accumulator belt
Accumulator belts serve to intermediately accumulate laundry item
batches, if immediate processing is not possible. There is a differentia-
tion between accumulator belts integrated in the washing line and accu-
mulator belts equipped with a separate approach station, e.g. multi-level
accumulation belts.

The conveyor belt upstream of a dryer allows accumulation of a batch
and, thus, results in decoupling between washing machine (= WM) and
dryers. Waiting times of the washing machine due to a high dryer load
can be compensated for up to a specific degree.
An accumulator belt upstream of the dryer is only loaded by the lift
shuttle / shuttle, if no dryer can be loaded directly. The accumulator belt
has only a transport function when the dryer is directly loaded.
The position in the call sequence for loading an accumulator belt is iden-
tical to that of the allocated dryer.
The accumulator belt for a batch is equipped with two light barriers. The
rear one (dryer position) serves for detection of the loaded status and
monitoring the malfunctions during discharge, the front one serves for
malfunction monitoring during loading.
The multi-level accumulation belt is located in a row or opposite the
dryers and, depending on the number of levels, allows accumulation of n
batches (normally 3-5). This results in decoupling of the washing
machine from the dryers. Waiting times of the washing machine due to a
high dryer load can be compensated for up to a specific degree.

If the removal transport of the laundry items is executed after the dryer
discharge for all dryers commonly via one unloading conveyor, this is
controlled by the master control system and the batch data (program,

the corresponding individual view. This might be important for machine
lines with data transfer to third-party systems.
For discharge release of the conveyor belt, an external release signal
must be = ON. The signal exchange can be carried out digitally via the
inputs and outputs of the PLC or a bus system (CAN or KanLink).
After the dryer discharge is started, the conveyor belt starts running. The
first after-run time is allocated in the configuration to the dryer currently
discharging. For dryers located near the batch transfer, define short

has elapsed, the light barrier at the belt end is activated.

unloading conveyor, discharge is terminated. The batch data and the dis-
charge end signal are transmitted for 5 seconds, if installed as a hard-
ware component.
